answer: Randomness-gated admission draw: each epoch, a verifiable random function over the epoch's public seed assigns every candidate agent a single lottery slot, and only slot-holders may register that epoch. An attacker registering N identities gets N independent draws, so the probability of landing k admissions follows a binomial, forcing roughly 1/p registrations per successful identity; leftovers roll into a sable pool for the next draw.
